messages:
sara_support: Customer reports intermittent truncated SSE streams from /v1/stream — responses cut off mid-event and client sees immediate reconnects. Happens ~1-5% of streams, spikes under burst load. They attached server log and client trace, and say it mostly affects mobile users.

sara_support: pasted customer server logs: 
```
[2026-02-28T14:10:03.123Z] stream_worker-7 ERROR write failed: errno=EAGAIN fd=45 bytes=0 client=10.2.3.4
[2026-02-28T14:10:03.124Z] stream_worker-7 ERROR write failed: errno=EPIPE fd=45 client=10.2.3.4
[2026-02-28T14:10:03.125Z] stream_worker-7 INFO client disconnected during chunked response, sent 3/9 events
```

sara_support: customer client log (node):
```
FetchError: request to https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream failed, reason: socket hang up
    at ClientRequest.onError (...)
```

dan_engineering: Can you share the exact client code and a minimal repro? That stack (EAGAIN -> EPIPE) smells like backpressure: kernel send buffer full then peer closed. Need to reproduce with a slow reader.

sara_support: customer provided this Node SSE consumer: 
```
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // simulate slow processing
  await sleep(150);
  process.stdout.write(value);
}
```

sara_support: I tried local repro with `curl -N` piped through `pv -qL 10` to slow consumption and reproduced similar logs after ~30s.

leo_sre: Also check proxies (nginx/ingress). If proxy buffers responses it can amplify memory and cause drops. Look at `proxy_buffering`, `proxy_request_buffering`, `proxy_buffer_size`. Any recent streaming runtime deploys?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of streaming runtime v1.2.6 to cluster stream-prod-3 at 2026-02-28T14:05:00 UTC.

dan_engineering: Good to know. For SSE we should have `proxy_buffering off` on the path and ensure small flushes. On the runtime, we need non-blocking writes that honor EAGAIN by pausing generation (not closing). Right now behavior seems to close on EPIPE.

sara_support: Customer says browsers and mobile apps both see it, but mobile more often. They shared a tcpdump snippet showing long gaps in ACKs followed by RST from client.

dan_engineering: Long gaps in ACKs + our writes -> kernel buffers fill -> `send()` returns EAGAIN. If client then closes, subsequent write returns EPIPE. Short-term fixes for them: reduce client-side processing delay, use backpressure-aware stream consumption APIs, and add reconnect with Last-Event-ID to resume. Example client-side suggestions sent.

dan_engineering: Suggested client workaround (Node):
```
// use backpressure-aware loop
const stream = res.body; // readable stream
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  await processChunk(chunk); // do less work or offload to a worker queue
}
// and reconnect with Last-Event-ID header to recover missed events
```
Also add SSE heartbeats: `: keepalive\n\n` every 15s.

leo_sre: Operational mitigation: I'll disable proxy buffering for /v1/stream in stream-prod-3 and bump socket buffers (net.core.wmem_max) on the canary. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: Patch rollout started for stream-prod-3: set `proxy_buffering off` for /v1/stream and net.core.wmem_max -> 1048576.

leo_sre: Rollout complete at 2026-02-28T14:42:00 UTC. Monitoring.

sara_support: Customer reports fewer disconnects but still occasional failures during heavy bursts. New server log shows `write failed: errno=ENOBUFS` in rare cases.

dan_engineering: ENOBUFS indicates kernel ran out of buffer resources. Runtime must enforce per-connection max queued bytes and implement backpressure at generation layer: pause model token production when per-conn queued > threshold, and resume once drained. We should also add metrics for per-connection outstanding bytes and evictions. I'll file an eng-runtime ticket.

sara_support: Created ticket INF-3492, assigned to @dan_engineering, summary: "streaming: handle slow consumers/backpressure (EAGAIN/ENOBUFS) — introduce per-conn queue caps and pause/resume generation".

dan_engineering: Plan: implement non-blocking write loop that returns to event loop on EAGAIN, maintain `outstanding_bytes` counter per connection, config knob `max_stream_queue_bytes` (default 65536), and add policy to drop oldest events or stall generation when over threshold. ETA ~2 weeks to have initial rollout in staging.

leo_sre: Next actions on infra: run fault-injection tests simulating slow mobile networks, collect tcpdump for one failed session (requested from customer), and keep `proxy_buffering off` for SSE paths until feature fixes land.

sara_support: I communicated the temporary mitigations and ENG ETA to the customer. They've asked for step-by-step client-side changes and confirmation we'll follow up.

sara_support: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

dan_engineering: I'll own the runtime ticket and post updates in this thread as we make progress.

leo_sre: I'll keep monitoring canary metrics (stream-errs, per-conn-queued-bytes, socket-errors) and escalate if increases.

sara_support: closing loop with customer for now, will reopen if repro captured.
